conventions.convention: Event and censoring times are finite, nonnegative real-valued random variables. Right censoring records U=min(T,C) and δ=1{T≤C}; event–censor ties count as events.
Left censoring records T≤L; interval censoring records L<T≤R; current status records 1{T≤C}; delayed entry selects T>L; right truncation selects T<R.

The right-censoring likelihood is conditional on observed Z, with product parameter space Θ×H, conditionally independent event and censor times, parameter-distinct laws, a Lebesgue event density, and one fixed sigma-finite censor dominator.

Sθ(u|z)=P(T>u|z), whereas Gη(u|z)=P(C≥u|z). Conditional identities hold almost everywhere in z separately for each parameter pair; no common exceptional set across uncountably many parameters is asserted.

Delayed-entry likelihoods condition on inclusion and observed entry. Random entry is independent of T given pre-entry W under a parameter-distinct entry law; Sθ(L|W)>0 is required. Events occur strictly after L, but censoring at L is allowed and has survivor ratio one.

load_bearing.statement: Under right censoring, the recorded pair is U=min(T,C) and δ=1{T≤C}. Left truncation selects only T>L; right truncation selects only T<R. A random observation endpoint is noninformative here only when fixed by design or independent of T conditional on the stated covariates under a parameter-distinct law.

Under AC and Countable Choice and the stated conditional independence, product-parameter, measurability and domination hypotheses, the conditional right-censored branch densities are hθ,η(u,1|z)=fθ(u|z)Gη(u|z) and hθ,η(u,0|z)=Sθ(u|z)gη(z,u). For an arbitrary event law, interval, left-censored and singleton probabilities are respectively Fθ(R|z)−Fθ(L|z), Fθ(L|z), and Fθ(t|z)−Fθ(t−|z). Fixed or noninformative inspection gives the stated event factors. Under the specified positive-probability delayed-entry model, conditional event and survivor terms are divided by Sθ(L|W); under positive-probability right truncation, the event law is restricted to T<R and normalized by P(T<R|Z=z).

seams_checked.note: The theorem identifies the subject unit, full times, observed record and conditional experiment, and preserves the contract's distinction between mathematical assumptions and empirical adequacy.

The survival definition uses nonnegative event times and S(t)=P(T>t). The censored exponential theorem preserves event-at-tie recording and separately states independence, parameter distinction and common domination.
The estimator definition and cited theorem facts retain δ=1{T≤C}, inclusive pre-event risk sets and baseline events. Independence and positive support are additional assumptions.

The score definition restates the same observation and tie conventions. It explicitly adds the conditional uniform-subset model rather than deriving exchangeability or a martingale contract from censoring conventions.

The Cox definition cites the same right-censoring map and tie rule. History-conditional independence and counting-process assumptions are stated separately; no conditional kernel given the entire covariate path is inferred.

The competing-risk definition and Aalen–Johansen procedure preserve event-at-censoring ties, inclusive risk counts and possible baseline events. Population interpretation requires separately stated independent censoring and support assumptions.
